search_space: All 8 labeled simple undirected graphs on the fixed vertex set {0,1,2}, with m fixed to 3. For each graph, the complete permutation group generated by its edge transpositions was enumerated, every group element was tested for order 3, and every ordered triple of distinct vertices was tested for a graph cycle of length 3.
witness_description: For m = 3, take the labeled simple graph with vertices {0,1,2} and edges {{0,1},{0,2}}. Its edge transpositions generate the 3-cycle (0 2 1), so they generate a cyclic subgroup of order 3, but the graph has no cycle of length 3.
refutation_explanation: Under right-to-left composition, (0 1) composed with (0 2) is the permutation (0 2 1), which has order 3. Thus the generated group contains its cyclic subgroup of order 3. The graph has only two edges and lacks the edge {1,2}, so it contains no 3-cycle; this falsifies the implication at m = 3.
